2027 Hyundai Porter Drops Cab-Over Design, Super-Cab Prototype Shows Long Bed
30 photos
Photo: Baldauf
Known as the H-100 in certain markets, the fourth-generation Porter is a very old truck. Hyundai launched it 22 years ago with a distinctive cab-over design. For 2027, however, the cab-over-front-axle format is going the way of the dodo for a longer front end, resulting in a completely different profile.
Spotted in super-cab guise testing at high altitude in Europe, this full-electric prototype stops short of a conventional pickup truck hood. Its front end stops short of a conventional pickup truck hood. The camo is, unsurprisingly, thicker around the fascia and front corners, yet said camo thankfully doesn't cover the windshield.
Now sitting at a shallower angle, the windshield is joined by tall and upright side windows. The roof also runs almost flat, and each front corner exposes rectangular headlamp clusters. With the 2027 redesign, Hyundai favors a boxier aesthetic in lieu of the short and more curvaceous fascia of the outgoing model.
Adding a noticeable step between the cabin and front of the vehicle, the nose is complemented by a long bed. While a conventional pickup spreads the front structure and cab over a longer body, light commercial vehicles like this one have to balance occupant protection without giving away too much space its owner gets paid to use.
With the longer nose, the front corners shift farther away from the driver. Making the nose longer also means the front axle can be moved forward, leaving the cab slightly behind said axle without eating into the cargo area. This redesign clearly is a balancing act, and Hyundai appears to have balanced it perfectly.
Photo: Baldauf The semi-hood profile of the 2027 model gives Hyundai engineers more room to package an energy-absorbing structure, which is vital if the South Korean automaker wants to sell the next-gen Porter in the Old Continent. As with its predecessor, the biggest focus here is the bed's footprint. Such vehicles also have to work on narrow streets, and the Porter does look a lot narrower than a van-derived flatbed such as the Euro-centric Ford Transit Dropside.
As far as this prototype is concerned, the work-first priorities are especially obvious from the very plain-looking bedsides and tailgate. Its cargo area visually separates from the passenger cell, indicating a body-on-frame design engineered to handle commercial payloads. Alongside the redesigned exterior, Hyundai is also giving the Porter a techy interior and new powertrain options.
The charging connection of the super-cabbed prototype confirms full electrification, yet combustion options are clearly happening as well. Its frame reads "4WD" as well, meaning that Hyundai is considering at least one dual-motor electric powertrain. As for what actually lies inside the Porter's cab, the biggest change for 2027 is the adoption of Pleos Connect infotainment.
Regarding the rest of the dash, look forward to a modernized layout with a cleaner, more techy aesthetic, digital instrument cluster and all. The bigger question, however, is whether Hyundai can find a way to retain the center armrest seat.
